display_name: Onesiphorus, one of the Three Hundred Alamanoi

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Ονησιφόρος, Παμμέγιστος, Παμφοδίτης, Παφνούτιος, Πηγών, Πολέμιος, Σωζόμενος, Σωτήριχος και Φώτιος», with the rank word left off; its page heading for him is «Αγιος Ονησιφορος». The company's own name as the page gives it is «οι 300 Άγιοι Αλαμανοί», and the English epithet in the display name is that company, which the page is the authority for.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Ονησιφόρος, Παμμέγιστος, Παμφοδίτης, Παφνούτιος, Πηγών, Πολέμιος, Σωζόμενος, Σωτήριχος και Φώτιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives each of the nine a heading of its own — his is «Αγιος Ονησιφορος» — so this is a synaxis that enumerates its members and is nine folders and not one. What the page says about them it says once, under all nine names: «Άγιοι της Εκκλησίας της Κύπρου, που συμπεριλαμβάνονται στους 300 Αγίους Αλαμανούς» — saints of the Church of Cyprus, who are counted among the three hundred holy Alamanoi. That is the whole of it. He is none of the corpus's three other men of this name: `onesiphorus-of-colophon`, the apostle of the Seventy, stands on 7 Σεπτεμβρίου; `onesiphorus-martyr-9-november` on 9 Νοεμβρίου; and `onesiphorus-of-anarita`, the ascetic of Paphos in Cyprus, on 13 Ιουλίου — that last is also Cypriot and was drafted five days before this one in this same wave, which makes the distinction worth saying plainly: his page gives him a cave at Anarita, an apolytikion and the Augustalios's career, while this man's page gives nothing at all but a name in a list of nine. No corpus folder of this name stands on 18 Ιουλίου in any calendar: the corpus keeps only `john-the-long-suffering` on this civil day and four more on the menologion's 18/7, and none of them belongs to this company. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on this page — the day's «Άγιος Ιωάννης Θ' Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης *», /2155/, does carry it and is refused. The page gives no year, no birthplace, no rank beyond Άγιος, no manner of death and no hymn, so there is no `dates` object, no `locations` and no `types`; the only further thing it prints is that a portion of this saint's relic is kept at the monastery of Kykkos in Cyprus, «Απότμημα του Ιερού Λειψάνου του Αγίου Ονησιφόρου βρίσκεται στη Μονή Κύκκου Κύπρου», and Cyprus is a whole island rather than a place of life the page states, so it is not taken as a location either.
